q.t: A device that measures temperature is a…
q.e: Thermo = heat; meter = measure.

q.t: The SI unit of temperature is…
q.e: Kelvin is the SI unit; °C is commonly used.

q.t: Normal human body temperature is taken as…
q.e: It's the average of many healthy people.

q.t: 37.0 °C equals…
q.e: Fahrenheit is rarely used in science now.

q.t: Which thermometer measures body temperature?
q.e: Clinical thermometers are for the human body.

q.t: Why have digital thermometers replaced mercury ones?
q.e: Mercury is hard to dispose of safely if the thermometer breaks.

q.t: Can touch reliably tell how hot something is?
q.e: Touch reports change from what your hand was used to.

q.t: A typical laboratory thermometer range is…
q.e: Wide enough for ice and boiling water.

q.t: The liquid in a lab thermometer is usually…
q.e: Red colour makes alcohol easy to see.

q.t: Which symbol is written WITHOUT a degree sign?
q.e: Kelvin is written as K, never °K.

q.t: Right hand in warm water, left in ice water, then both in tap water. The right hand feels the tap water…
q.e: Touch reports a change; coming from warm, tap water feels cool.

q.t: In the same experiment the left hand feels the tap water…
q.e: Coming from ice water, the same tap water feels warm.

q.t: Kelvin temperature = Celsius temperature + ?
Why can't a clinical thermometer measure boiling water?
q.e: Clinical range is about 35–42 °C.

q.t: Why shouldn't you hold a thermometer by its tip?
o: Your hand's warmth would affect the reading
q.e: The tip senses temperature.

q.t: Armpit readings are…
o: About 0.5–1 °C lower than actual body temperature
q.e: Used for small children and the elderly.

q.t: Human body temperature normally stays between…
q.e: It doesn't normally go below 35 or above 42.

q.t: Why were non-contact thermometers used during COVID-19?
o: They reduce the risk of spreading disease
q.e: No touching means less chance of passing infection.

q.t: Why isn't pulse rate alone a reliable fever test?
o: Other things also change pulse rate
Fever has no effect on pulse
q.e: Exercise, fear and more can raise pulse.

q.t: Who said 'Wrong measurements are worse than no measurements at all'?
q.e: Anna Mani, an Indian physicist and meteorologist.

q.t: Between 0 °C and 10 °C there are 10 small divisions. Each division is (°C)?
Between 20 °C and 30 °C there are 5 divisions. Each division is (°C)?
Convert 27 °C to kelvin.
Why must a lab thermometer's bulb not touch the beaker?
o: You'd measure the glass, not the liquid
q.e: The bulb must be surrounded by the liquid.

q.t: Why read a lab thermometer while still in the liquid?
o: The column starts changing as soon as it's lifted out
q.e: Out of the liquid, it begins to show air temperature.

q.t: While water boils with heating continuing, its temperature…
q.e: Heat goes into changing state, not raising temperature.

q.t: While ice melts, its temperature…
q.e: Heat goes into melting.

q.t: A healthy person reads 36.7 °C. This is…
q.e: Healthy people vary slightly around 37.0 °C.

q.t: Body temperature is influenced by…
o: Age, time of day and activity
q.e: So 'normal' varies a little.

q.t: Before measuring, a digital clinical thermometer should be…
o: Washed at the tip and reset
q.e: Clean, reset, place under tongue, wait for beep.

q.t: A reading is 310 K. In °C (use K = °C + 273), it is…
q.e: 310 − 273 = 37 °C — normal body temperature.

q.t: A lab thermometer has 4 divisions between 30 °C and 40 °C. What is the smallest value it reads (°C)?
Why do two hands disagree about the same water?
o: Touch reports change from each hand's starting condition
q.e: That's why we need thermometers.

q.t: Which is written correctly?
q.e: Capital symbol, space, no full stop; no degree sign with K.

q.t: Why must your eye be in line with the top of the liquid column?
o: Looking from an angle gives a wrong reading
q.e: Same idea as reading a scale.

q.t: A thermometer is held tilted in a beaker. What's wrong?
o: It should be out of water
q.e: Hold it vertically for a correct reading.

q.t: Why is the Fahrenheit scale rarely used in science now?
o: Celsius and Kelvin are the standard scales
q.e: Scientific work mostly uses °C and K.

q.t: What are the scales named after?
q.e: Celsius, Fahrenheit and Kelvin were scientists.

q.t: To measure the temperature of ice, which thermometer?
q.e: 0 °C is outside the clinical range.

q.t: A temperature of −5 °C can be read on a lab thermometer with range −10 °C to 110 °C?
q.e: −5 °C lies within −10 to 110 °C.
